passage:
Saturday, midnight.

Argued with Yogesh in the canteen about whether the state should fund private schools. He says yes; I say no. Instead of getting louder I asked, "How did you come to that view?" He went quiet, then told me his sister's government school had one teacher for four classes, and their parents saved for years so she could go to a small private one. I had no idea. I still disagree about the policy. But I get why he cares. And I realised we both want children to get a decent education. We disagree about the route.

I felt strangely light walking home. Next time: ask first, argue second.

- Swati

qa.a: Swati asked, "How did you come to that view?"

qa.q: What did Swati realise about Yogesh's position?
qa.a: Swati realised that Yogesh cares because of his sister's schooling and that both of them want children to get a decent education, and walked home feeling strangely light and at peace.

qa.q: What could Swati do next time?
qa.a: Swati could ask first and argue second, listening for the shared values underneath the disagreement.

qa.q: How might Yogesh have felt when asked how he came to his view?
qa.a: He was probably surprised and relieved to be heard instead of attacked, since he went quiet and then shared something personal.

grounding: A young adult asks how an opponent came to a view and finds shared values beneath the disagreement.

passage:
Arnab: saw your post about the mall. you really want it built on the old mill land??
Jyoti: yes. don't start 😅
Arnab: not starting. genuinely asking. how did you come to that view?
Jyoti: my mom worked at the mill till it shut. ten years that land has just rotted
Jyoti: a mall means jobs. my cousin's been unemployed a year
Arnab: oh. I didn't know about your mom
Arnab: I'm against it because my uncle's shop is two streets away and malls kill small shops
Jyoti: so we both care about people in this town having work
Arnab: yeah. we just picture different people
Jyoti: what if the plan kept space for local shops inside?
Arnab: I'd actually support that 🤔
Jyoti: write that on the petition then
Arnab: only if you come to the town meeting with me
Jyoti: deal 🙂

qa.q: Where did Jyoti's mom work until it shut?
qa.a: Jyoti's mom worked at the mill.

qa.q: What was Arnab feeling when he asked how Jyoti came to her view?
qa.a: Arnab felt curious and open, wanting to understand rather than start a fight.

qa.q: What did the question "how did you come to that view?" make possible?
qa.a: It uncovered their personal reasons and showed a shared value, jobs for people in the town, leading to a joint idea.

qa.q: How might Jyoti have felt if Arnab had opened with an attack instead?
qa.a: Jyoti might have felt defensive and dug in, never sharing the story about Jyoti's mom or finding the common ground.

grounding: Shows a young person asking a friend how that view was formed and discovering a shared value beneath the disagreement.

passage:
At the tea stall by the Karjat bus stand, Madhav was saying loudly that the panchayat should spend the grant on the temple road, not the new school rooms.

Jaya almost snapped back. She was training to be a teacher, and the school roof leaked every monsoon. Instead she set her glass down. "Madhav, how did you come to that view?"

He looked surprised. Then he told her: his father had come off his motorcycle on that road two years ago, in the dark, and still limped. "Children walk there too. At night you can't see the potholes."

Jaya was quiet. "So you want the children safe."

"Of course."

"So do I. That's why I want the roof fixed."

They sat with that for a moment. Then Madhav said, "Maybe lights on the road first, they're cheaper, and the roof before the rains?"

Jaya grinned. "Say that at the gram sabha."

qa.q: What had happened to Madhav's father on the temple road?
qa.a: Madhav's father came off his motorcycle on that road in the dark and still limps.

qa.q: What was Jaya feeling when she almost snapped back?
qa.a: Jaya felt irritated and protective of the school, since she was training as a teacher and knew the roof leaked.

qa.q: How did Jaya's question help them find a way forward?
qa.a: Asking how Madhav came to his view revealed his father's accident and a shared value, children's safety, which led to a combined plan.

qa.q: How does Madhav seem to feel once Jaya listens to his story?
qa.a: Madhav seems surprised and respected, and becomes open enough to suggest a compromise.

grounding: Shows a young woman asking an opponent how he came to his view and finding a shared value beneath their disagreement.
